newsitem.title: GERMANY: DASA in pact with Lagardere.
newsitem.headline: DASA in pact with Lagardere.

text.p: Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA) and France's Lagardere said on Wednesday they had reached a strategic cooperation agreement covering missiles, space and defence electronics.

In a statement issued by DASA's Munich headquarters, the two companies said DASA would offer its "total and unconditional support" for Lagardere's bid to buy Thomson-CSF, which is being offered for privatisation in France.

The statement said that the signing of the cooperation deal between DASA, a unit of auto giant Daimler-Benz, and defence-to-missiles group Lagardere was vital in the face of mounting North American competition.

"This Europe-wide consolidation is of critical necessity in order to be able to face increasing competition from the American industry, which has already been restructured into a few major groups," the joint statement said.
The signing of memorandum of understanding also widens Lagardere's partnerships beyond its existing alliances with British Aerospace and GEC, it added.
The statement added that the strategic cooperation would take place in three key areas:

-- SPACE: The activities of Matra Marconi Space -- a joint venture between Lagardere and GEC -- will be combined with DASA's. The cooperation would cover satellites, launch vehicles and orbital infrastructure. DASA and MMS will be equal partners in a business which will have worldwide sales of $3 billion.
-- MISSILES: Matra BAe Dynamics -- a joint venture between Lagardere and British Aerospace -- will take a 30 percent stake in DASA unit LFK and become its strategic partner.
-- DEFENCE ELECTRONICS: Lagardere and DASA intend to combine certain areas of their defence electronics businesses in several steps to create a company of equal partners.
Earlier, Lagardere and French engineering group Alcatel Alsthom said they had both submitted firm and final offers to buy the 58 percent state holding in Thomson-CSF.
British Aerospace said it had put 300 million pounds ($490.5 million) into the Lagardere offer, while GEC had signed memoranda of understanding with both bidders.
-- Douglas Busvine, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
